chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from al-Faḍl Abī al-ʿAbbās, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the leftover water of the cat, the sheep, the cow, the camel, the donkey, the horse, the mules, wild animals, and predatory beasts. I did not leave anything without asking him about it, and he said: “There is no harm in it.”
Until I came to the dog, so he said: “It is filthy and impure. Do not perform wudu (ablution) with its leftover water. Pour out that water and wash it with earth the first time, then with water.”

key_terms.بِالتُّرَابِ: with earth or soil as part of cleansing
key_terms.فَضْلِ: leftover water or remainder from which an animal has drunk

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on using the leftover water of animals, especially a dog, for wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the leftover water of various animals. It states that the leftover water of many animals is unobjectionable, but the dog's leftover water is najis and may not be used for wudu (ablution), and the vessel is to be cleansed with earth first and then with water.
